rounds.text: Aarnav Fashions Ltd trades at a notable discount to its asset base, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.76x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.28x [E2, E7]. This deep asset discount is paired with robust multi-year profit acceleration, demonstrated by a 175% compounded profit growth over 3 years and 77% over 10 years [E18, E20]. Fundamental performance has clearly outpaced the stock price over the medium term, as 5-year profit grew 14% while the price dropped 11% [E53]. Furthermore, a discounted cash model indicates substantial intrinsic undervaluation, offering a margin of safety of 45.3% at the current market price of ₹ 35.2 [E43, E44]. The reverse DCF shows that the current price prices in a modest 5.7% earnings growth, which sits well below the base case assumption of 14.0% [E45]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth declined by 2% and sales dropped 11% YoY [E21, E67].

The most critical vulnerability for Aarnav Fashions Ltd is the sharp reversal in its short-term earnings momentum, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -2% [E21] alongside year-over-year sales contracting by 11% [E67]. This fundamental cooling is further confirmed by screening mechanisms flagging explicit deceleration in earnings growth [E68]. While long-term profit growth figures look impressive historically [E18], the immediate operational reality shows the company trading at a P/E of 16.15x, which represents a premium over the sector benchmark of 15.93x [E6]. Compounding these operational headwinds and premium multiple is a total absence of shareholder cash returns, evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: [E43].

The bear’s focus on short-term contraction ignores the company’s massive long-term compounding power, where profit growth has reached 77% over ten years [E18] and 175% over the last three years [E20]. While the bear highlights a -2% TTM profit dip [E21] and -11% sales decline [E67], these figures are dwarfed by the company’s 15.4% median sales growth over the last decade [E57]. The claim that the stock is expensive is contradicted by the fact that it trades at a significant discount to its book value, with a P/B of 0.75x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.28x [E7]. Conceded: [E4], [E6], and [E68]. Furthermore, the market is currently pricing in only 5.7% growth, which is far below the 14% base case assumption, suggesting that the current valuation is overly pessimistic [E45]. This disconnect between fundamental performance and market price is confirmed by the scanX signal engine, which notes that fundamentals have been outpacing the stock price over the last five years [E53].

The bull relies on historical profit figures like 77% over ten years [E18] and 175% over three years [E20] to mask current deterioration, but ignores the reality that trailing twelve-month profit growth has already turned negative at -2% [E21]. While the bull points to a 15.4% median sales growth over the decade [E57], this historical tailwind stands in stark contrast to the screen reason highlighting a severe -11% year-over-year sales decline [E67]. Conceded: [E7]. The bull’s reliance on backward-looking book value and low expectations overlooks clear evidence that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E68]. Furthermore, citing a multi-year fundamental outperformance [E53] does nothing to excuse the immediate operational contraction evidenced by falling sales [E67] and shrinking trailing profits [E21].
